sentences.text: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI
ORAL ORDER (PER: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI)

In this petition filed under section 439 of Cr.P.C./483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short, 'BNSS'), the petitioner who is arraigned as accused No.9 is seeking bail in Crime No.120/2024 of Gokak Rural Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 489A, 489B, 489C and 420 of IPC.
2. In support of the petition, the petitioner has contended that he is innocent of the offences alleged and having valid and tenable defence.
There is no material to show that he is indulged in counterfeiting of currency notes or using counterfeit notes as genuine.
He was not found in possession of any counterfeit currency notes.
No material on equipment relating to printing of counterfeit notes has been seized from the petitioner.
There are no allegations that petitioner is trying to escape from the Police when intercepted at Konnur NC: 2024:KHC-D:13098 Railway Station Bridge.
Even as per the mahazar, the seized articles do not bear the mark of reserve Bank of India.
Rather they bear the mark Children's Bank of India.
The seized articles are not counterfeit currency notes, but material used for educational purpose used by the school projects by the children.
Petitioner is the sole earning member of the family.
He is handicap.

On account of arrest,
the entire family members are suffering.
Petitioner is ready and willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and offers substantial surety to the satisfaction of the trial court and hence, the petition.

3. Learned HCGP submitted oral objections stating that on 28.06.2024 at 11.00 p.m., on receipt of credible information, the complainant intercepted a white car bearing registration No.KA-22/G-1075, coming from Court Circle side Kadabagatti-Kanasageri Road near Sri Chowdeshwari Temple, accused Nos.1 to NC: 2024:KHC-D:13098 5 were found in the said car.
In the said car, a black bag containing notes of 100 and 500 denominations were found bearing the mark Children's Bank of India.
The accused persons disclosed that they would exchange these notes in the ratio of 4:1 per genuine currency.
Therefore, accused Nos.1 to 5 were arrested and the counterfeit notes found with them are seized.
Later, accused Nos.6 to 10 are arrested and remanded to custody.
From the possession of the accused, car bearing registration No.KA-38/M-6049 and five bundles of blank papers of the size of 500 denomination currency notes and two cell phones are seized.
If released on bail, there is likelihood of the petitioner indulging in similar offence and may also abscond and prays to reject the petition.

4. Heard the arguments and perused the records.

sentences.text: According to the prosecution, on 28.6.2024 at 11.00 p.m., on receipt of credible information, the complainant along with his staff intercepted a white car bearing registration number KA-22/-G-1075, coming from Court Circle side on Kadabagatti-Kanasageri Road near Sri Chowdeshwari Temple.
Accused Nos.1 to 5 were found in the said car.
In the said car, a black bag containing notes of 100 and 500 denominations were found bearing the mark Children's Bank of India.
The accused persons disclosed that they would exchange these notes in the ratio of 4:1 per genuine currency.
Therefore, accused Nos.1 to 5 were arrested and the counterfeit notes found with them are seized.
Later, accused Nos.6 to 10 are arrested and remanded to custody.
From the possession of the accused, car bearing registration number KA-38/M-6049 and five bundles of blank papers of the size of 500 denomination currency notes and two cell phones are seized.

As per the prosecution case, what is found in possession of the accused persons are certain notes containing the mark Children's bank of India, which appears to be used for school projects by the students.
From the description of the seized articles, it appears to be the material required by the students for carrying on the school projects and also children used for playing.

Other than the allegations that the currency notes bearing the mark Children's Bank of India, no other articles were found which indicate that the accused persons are indulged in counterfeiting currency notes.
The petitioner is produced before the trial court with the application seeking judicial custody which indicates that no longer his custody is required for the purpose of investigation.
Of course, there is apprehension that the petitioner may abscond and also threaten or temper with the witnesses which may be overcome by imposing conditions.

In the above circumstances, this court is of NC:
2024:KHC-D:13098 the considered opinion that petitioner is entitled for bail and accordingly, the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Petitioner/accused No.9 is released on bail in Crime No.120/2024 of Gokak Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under Sections 120B, 489A, 489B, 489C and 420 of IPC, subject to following:
CONDITIONS a) The petitioner/accused No.9

shall execute a personal bond in a sum of 50,000/-
with one surety for the like-sum to the satisfaction of the trial court.
b) He shall make himself available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and he shall co-operate with the investigation.

c) He shall furnish his residential address proof and shall inform the investigating NC:
2024:KHC-D:13098 officer/Court if there is any change in the address.
d) He shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
